newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia poll results must be respected -- government.
newsitem.headline: Serbia poll results must be respected -- government.

text.p: The Serbian government seemed to cave in on Saturday to demands that opposition victories at disputed local elections be restored, agreeing with Belgrade students that November poll results must be respected.

"The Serbian government representatives agreed with the necessity that the will of the citizens expressed at local elections must be fully respected," said a statement signed by two Serbian deputy prime ministers and a delegation of student protesters.

"In keeping with this, the government will during the day order the Justice Ministry to demand of competent state bodies, which still have not finished establishing final election results, to do this as soon as possible," the statement said.

The opposition Zajedno coalition claimed it won in 14 of Serbia's 18 largest cities including the capital Belgrade and the second city, Nis, but Milosevic's Socialists annulled the victories, claiming unspecified irregularities. The cancellation triggered a wave of daily street protests by Belgrade students and Zajedno supporters, now in their eighth week.

Earlier this week the Serbian government ordered the election commission in Nis to concede his party's election loss there. "The competent state bodies will be demanded also to determine responsibility and adequate punishment in cases where election results were forged," the statement said.
The statement came hours after political sources had said Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic was expected to acknowledge opposition victories in the elections and call for a coalition government.
